notes:
Account background: Lucent Loop builds a VS Code 'assistant' extension targeted at mid-size engineering teams who want enterprise controls. Extension offers inline suggestions, multi-line streaming completion, and a contextual search of monorepos. They are very sensitive to per-keystroke latency — stated goal: "sub-50ms inline suggestions, P95 <100ms during normal load".

Technical requirements (callouts):
- Streaming completions with partial-token flush so suggestions start appearing immediately; prefer server-sent events / gRPC streaming demo.
- Model & version pinning for reproducible CI/code-gen across releases (must be able to lock model+quant config per-extension release).
- Per-developer and per-org rate limits + burst allowances; UX should gracefully degrade with fallbacks, not show errors.
- Low token cost is important; will evaluate Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching and KV prefix caching.
- Need audit logs for developer queries and optional redaction for sensitive repo paths.

Security/compliance:
- They require SSO (SAML) + SCIM provisioning, KMS integration for encryption at rest, and 1-year audit log retention (must be configurable). Some repos flagged as sensitive require VPC/private deployment or on-premise agents.

Pilot scope proposed: 2-week POC using Dedicated pool (small GPU reserve), integrate extension with Redwood streaming endpoint, measure latency & P95 under 50 concurrent devs, verify model pinning flow in CI, and validate audit logs.

Direct quote from CTO (paraphrased): "If we can get suggestions to feel instantaneous and avoid ghost typing when rate limits kick in, we can scale adoption across our developer base."

Commercial notes:
- Preference toward reserved capacity deal if latency targets met.
- Price sensitivity: wants cap on token spend per-month for pilot.

Open items: security signoff timeline, legal DPA, exact SLO numbers for pilot, egress/firewall requirements for hosted vs private deployment.
